_comment: Every component that ships inside a release artifact, with a resolved license disposition.
tools/audit_notices.py compares this against the distributions actually installed into the
release runtime environment, so a new bundled dependency fails the build until it is given a
disposition here and an attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Licenses are taken from each distribution's own published metadata and license files, not from
a summary. 'license' is the SPDX identifier for what is relied on; where a project offers a
choice, 'license_choice_note' records which arm was taken.

python_distributions.name: cryptography
python_distributions.license_choice_note: Offered as 'Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause'; Apache-2.0 is taken so it matches this project's own license.
python_distributions.copyright: Copyright (c) Individual contributors to the cryptography project

embeds.name: OpenSSL
embeds.note: The cryptography Windows wheel statically links OpenSSL 3.x, which is Apache-2.0.

python_distributions.name: pillow
python_distributions.copyright: Copyright (c) 1997-2011 by Secret Labs AB, Copyright (c) 1995-2011 by Fredrik Lundh and contributors; Pillow is Copyright (c) 2010-2025 by Jeffrey A. Clark and contributors

python_distributions.name: pystray
python_distributions.note: The only copyleft component in a release artifact. Its source headers grant version 3 of the LGPL 'or, at your option, any later version', so the identifier is -or-later rather than the bare 'LGPLv3' in its wheel metadata. Its wheel declares COPYING and COPYING.LGPL as license files but ships neither, so the text is carried in LICENSES/ instead. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for the obligations this creates.

python_distributions.name: pywin32
python_distributions.license_choice_note: The wheel's classifier says 'Python Software Foundation License', but the license text it actually ships (win32/License.txt) is a three-clause BSD form naming Mark Hammond. The shipped text is what is reproduced and relied on.

cannot be enumerated from the lock. These are reviewed against a real onedir tree rather than
assumed; see TODO.md for the artifact-level audit that closes the remaining native libraries.
